title: College Football Week 4 Picks: Spread Predictions, Odds & Betting Lines for Top 25 Games - CBS Sports
body:
The college football slate for Week 4 has quickly become the most compelling of the season, with a cluster of top‑25 matchups that promise to reshape the early‑year rankings and ignite betting interest across the nation. From a showdown between two Power Five titans to a high‑stakes rivalry that could determine conference supremacy, the weekend’s schedule offers more drama than a Hollywood script, and sportsbooks are already adjusting lines as analysts weigh injuries, home‑field advantage and recent form.

At the heart of the action is the clash between the No. 4 ranked Tigers and the No. 9 Hurricanes, a game that many pundits have labeled the “Game of the Week.” Both teams arrive with 2‑0 records, but the Tigers have leaned heavily on a balanced offense that averages 38 points per game, while the Hurricanes’ defense has surrendered just 14 points per contest. The spread, initially posted at Tigers –4.5, has tightened to –2.5 after a surge of early bets on the underdog, reflecting confidence in Miami’s ability to keep the contest within a single score. Analysts point to the Hurricanes’ revamped secondary and a newly installed zone blitz scheme as key factors that could stifle the Tigers’ aerial attack.

Another marquee pairing pits the No. 12 Wildcats against the No. 18 Broncos in a battle of contrasting styles. The Wildcats, led by a quarterback who has thrown for 1,200 yards and 12 touchdowns in the first two weeks, are favored by 7 points. However, the Broncos’ ground game, anchored by a running back who averages 7.5 yards per carry, has already racked up 250 rushing yards in just two outings. Betting markets have responded with a modest shift toward the Broncos, with the over/under hovering at 58.5 points—a figure that suggests a potentially high‑scoring affair if both offenses click.

Mid‑week, the rivalry between the No. 15 Bulldogs and the No. 22 Spartans offers a classic “defensive duel” narrative. Both squads rank among the nation’s top ten in total defense, and the line movement has been relatively static, keeping the Bulldogs at –3. The Spartans, however, have a veteran special teams unit that could swing momentum with a blocked kick or a return touchdown. Experts caution that the low-scoring nature of the teams’ recent games makes the over/under—set at 44.5—a risky proposition for bettors seeking big payouts.

Beyond the top‑25 matchups, several under‑the‑radar contests are drawing attention for their betting value. The upset‑prone Rams, currently unranked but boasting a 2‑0 start, are listed as +6.5 against the 21‑ranked Cougars, whose offense has stumbled in the first two weeks. The Rams’ aggressive play‑calling and a newly installed offensive line have been cited as reasons to consider the spread a “buy‑low” opportunity, especially as the Cougars’ starting quarterback sits out with a lingering ankle issue.

The weekend’s betting landscape also reflects a broader trend: sportsbooks are tightening lines earlier in the week as data-driven models incorporate real‑time injury reports and weather forecasts. For instance, the rain‑soaked field at the Lakeside Stadium has prompted a 0.5‑point adjustment in the spread for the home team’s game against a high‑powered offense, indicating that oddsmakers expect the conditions to slow down the aerial attack.

Looking ahead, the outcomes of these Week 4 battles will have ripple effects well beyond the immediate win‑loss columns. A victory for the Hurricanes could catapult them into the top three, forcing the Tigers to reevaluate their defensive schemes. Meanwhile, a surprise win by the Broncos would tighten the race for the conference’s coveted championship game berth, setting the stage for a dramatic second half of the season. As fans settle in for a weekend of gridiron fireworks, the betting community will be watching closely, ready to adjust strategies based on the results that could redefine the early narrative of the 2026 college football campaign.
